jobs.how: The supplement names no BMS run or enable point, so treat this as monitoring: read the status code, whether the boiler is available, and which inputs and priorities are active.
Map by object ID because several names repeat. The supplement gives no units, so check readings against the boiler display before trending or alarming on them.
All firing points are read-only. Compare the boiler's own modulation rate with the rate requested over the network, and use the gas valve relay bit as the burner-on signal.

points.use: Read: modulation rate requested over the network
Read: gas valve relay on (burner firing)
Read: target reduced for flue temperature
Read: target reduced for boiler in/out

jobs.how: Relay output bits show which circulators the boiler has energised; separate bits flag when a pump runs for exercise or freeze protection rather than for heat.

points.use: Read: circulator 1 on for freeze protection
Read: boiler circulator on for freeze protection

jobs.how: Alarm on the sensor warning code and the live bits for open limits, switches, sensor errors and gas valve faults. Lockout counters show how often the boiler has locked out.
Three lockout history blocks record the hard and soft error, a time stamp and the conditions at the time. LKHS1-3 bits break the errors out by cause.

points.use: Read: LKHS1 hard flame fault bit
Read: LKHS1 hard ignition fault bit
Read: LKHS1 hard high temp limit bit

jobs.how: These writable AVs are boiler configuration values, not a run command, and the supplement does not say which one a BMS should use as a setpoint. Change one only when adjusting setup, never cyclically.

points.use: Priority 1 supply max target; check it's writable on the controller
Priority 1 supply min target; check it's writable on the controller
Priority 1 OD reset/volts max; check it's writable on the controller
Priority 1 OD reset/volts min; check it's writable on the controller
WWSD temperature setting; check it's writable on the controller
High limit temperature setting; check it's writable on the controller
Outdoor temperature correction; check it's writable on the controller

jobs.how: The master block reports network totals and boiler order; Shadow 2-8 blocks repeat each other boiler's status. Rotation settings are writable configuration AVs.

points.use: Read: number of boilers on network
Boiler rotation method setting; check it's writable on the controller
Force lead rotate; check it's writable on the controller

checklist: Set the device instance, MAC address and baud rate on the ProtoNode using its start-up guide; the point supplement does not list them.
Set the ProtoNode for BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP; the same object list is served either way.
Discover the device and map by object ID, not name, because names repeat (MI 138 and AI 653 are both Boiler Status).
With the boiler running, verify reads of MI 138 (Boiler Status), AI 10 (target supply), AI 7 (outlet), AI 307 (modulation) and AI 19 (outdoor).
Confirm BI 594 (Relay Output Gas Valve ON) turns on when the burner fires and AI 307 rises.
Note the healthy values of AI 160 (Sensor Warnings) and BI 666-668 (sensor errors) before building alarms on them.
If a setting must change, write one AV such as AV 33 once and read it back; the supplement has no read/write column, so confirm it is writable, and never write AVs cyclically.
Map alarms on BI 661-665 (open limits and switches), BI 669 (gas valve fault) and AI 162/AI 163 (lockout history errors).
